thread:
devon: quick flag — on the EU private deployment we've got a spike of outbound to the metadata-ish IP from the keystore shim. noticed during a perf run, looks noisy. anyone seen this pattern?
anya: ugh, which IP exactly? metadata or our KMS?
devon: 169.254.169.254 repeated GETs, and a handful of connections to our internal keystore-proxy (10.2.4.8:8443). pattern is short-lived bursts every ~30s.
michael: can you paste a short snippet of the logs?
devon: sure — from the keystore agent on node-17: 
```
[2026-03-22T18:12:03Z] keystore-agent[pid=2123] DEBUG call=GetKey keystore_request_id=5f9a client=svc-inference
[2026-03-22T18:12:03Z] http: GET http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance/identity -> 200
[2026-03-22T18:12:03Z] proxy: dial tcp 10.2.4.8:8443 -> established
[2026-03-22T18:12:03Z] keystore-agent TRACE stack=keystore.Initialize->keystore.GetRemoteKey->auth.FetchIdentity
```
anya: hmm stacktrace shows auth.FetchIdentity called on every GetKey; we expected a cached identity token + KV cache. is caching disabled?
sara: devon, what's the deployment config for KEYSERVER_AUTH_CACHE_TTL?
devon: in the env for that cluster it's unset (we used defaults when bootstrapping).
anya: default should be 15m. if it's unset maybe fallback to 0. would explain the 30s bursts. can someone check the configmap?
ops-kate: i'm on it — checking now.
sec-bot: detected 127x auth calls in the last 10m from namespace priv-eu-prod; potential misconfiguration flagged. severity=low but noisy.
michael: aside from performance, this has isolation concerns — each auth call hits metadata IP which might be reachable only via certain netpols. if shims are calling host metadata frequently, could be an attack surface.
anya: agreed. immediate steps: (1) toggle KEYSERVER_AUTH_CACHE_TTL to 15m in the keystore configmap and rollout a canary, (2) add short-lived local token caching in agent codepath if not present, (3) audit RBAC so only keystore-agent SA can call the proxy endpoint.
devon: on (3) — current netpol allows pods in priv namespace to talk to 10.2.4.0/24:8443. we should tighten to only keystore-agent label selector.
sara: also add an audit log filter to the proxy: log every identity fetch with svcaccount + pod name + callstack. we need forensics if this reappears.
ops-kate: created PR to set KEYSERVER_AUTH_CACHE_TTL=15m in k8s/priv-keystore/values.yaml -> https://git.company/pr/1487, will canary to 2 nodes.
michael: for KMS integration questions — if we're relying on metadata for instance identity, document the threat model. maybe we should prefer mTLS handshake to the proxy instead of metadata bearer.
anya: yes doc that and capture the mitigation matrix: netpol scope, RBAC SA scoping, audit logs, local caching, and fallback rate limiter.
devon: vuln triage note — this could escalate if an attacker creates many pods with that SA and forces identity churn. I'll open a vuln ticket and label P2 until we validate scope.
sec-bot: ticket created: SEC-2026-321; assignees: devon, anya; due=2026-03-24.
sara: small quick test: devon can you run this on a canary pod and show before/after counts for metadata GETs? command: 
```
kubectl logs -n priv-eu-prod -l app=keystore-agent --since=15m | grep 169.254.169.254 | wc -l
```
devon: running now... before change: 124 hits in 15m. after cache TTL set and restarted agent on canary node: 3 hits in 15m. so TTL fixes the noise.
anya: nice. next: we'll prepare a follow-up to tighten netpol and RBAC in the next deploy window. please include audit log schema changes and a sample query for SRE to detect regressions (e.g., group by pod/serviceaccount, threshold >5/min).
michael: i'll draft the rollout playbook and add a rollback (set TTL back to 0) and test plan for evicted tokens.
ops-kate: rolling the netpol tighten as a separate PR to avoid coupling. link when ready.
devon: thanks all — summarizing: cache TTL fix deployed to canary, huge reduction in metadata egress; follow-ups: netpol tighten, RBAC SA scoping, proxy audit logs, agent caching hardening, and doc of threat model.
anya: ping @sara @michael for review of the audit schema.
sara: will review today. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: resolution=mitigated_temporarily; watch_window=48h; monitor_query="sum by (pod,svca) (rate(keystore_identity_fetches[5m])) > 5"
ops-kate: adding monitor to prod in a few mins.
michael: thanks — file closure once monitors look stable and PRs merged.
anya: closing loop: also include a note in the private-deploy checklist about verifying KEYSERVER_AUTH_CACHE_TTL when onboarding new clusters.
